info.title: Backprod API
info.description:
Every response that is not a success is the §10.4 envelope: one `error` object carrying a stable machine-readable `code`, a human `message`, a `details` object and the `request_id` to quote when asking about it. Driver text, SQL and stack traces never appear in it (§31), in any environment.

**Context is carried in headers, never in the body or the path.** `X-Product` names the product and `X-Tenant` the tenant; a tenant a caller is not a member of is refused rather than silently emptied, and a client-supplied tenant is never trusted as authority — it is checked against membership.

**Money is integer minor units with its currency beside it.** There are no floats: 1999 EUR is nineteen euros ninety-nine, and a rounding rule belongs to whoever formats it.

servers.description: The API is mounted at the root; every path below is absolute.

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Who the caller is, and what this product and tenant let them do.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Product discovery, which runs before a product is resolved.

tags.name: Catalogue
tags.description: Plans, features and the offers on sale.

tags.name: Subscription
tags.description: The tenant's subscription, its terms, and what it entitles them to.

tags.name: Billing
tags.description: Invoices, payments, credit notes and the e-invoicing transmissions that follow them.

tags.name: Tax
tags.description: Tax profiles, VAT regimes, the transactions they produce and the periods they are declared in (§25.3).

tags.name: Sales
tags.description: The commercial chain of non-negotiable #20: quote → order → invoice → subscription, traceable end to end.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: One event, many channels, consent-gated (§27.1). A suppression is a recorded outcome, never a silence.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: The first product resource: JSONB documents with versions.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: Files kept outside the database, reached by signed links.

tags.name: Geometry
tags.description: Spatial computation over caller-supplied GeoJSON (§19 phase 1). Behind the `gis.access` entitlement, backed by core PostgreSQL with no PostGIS dependency, and deliberately without a buffer operation — §19 names buffers among the things a spatial extension is for, and an approximation of one would be harder to remove than an endpoint that does not exist yet.

tags.name: Conversations
tags.description: Threads inside a tenant, and support threads that cross to the platform (§12.3).

tags.name: Tenants
tags.description: The tenant the caller is acting inside, and who belongs to it.

tags.name: Staff
tags.description: The platform's side of support. A different identity model from a tenant membership, and every read is recorded.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: Operations and finance. Strictly separated from anything a tenant can see (non-negotiable #19).

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description: Work taken off the request path (D3).

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Providers calling in. Each authenticates the request itself; there is no caller to authenticate.

bearerAuth.description: An RS256 access token from the identity provider, verified locally against its published keys. Swapping provider is an adapter change (ADR-014).

ProductHeader.name: X-Product
ProductHeader.description: Which product this request is about. Required on everything except discovery and the public surface — a resource endpoint without it is refused rather than guessed at (§12.1).

TenantHeader.name: X-Tenant
TenantHeader.description: Which tenant, when the caller belongs to more than one. Checked against membership, never believed on its own.

DirectoryLimit.name: limit
DirectoryLimit.description: Page size. A value outside the range is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED rather than clamped.

AccessPurpose.name: X-Access-Purpose
AccessPurpose.description:
Why this read is happening, as the log can count it (R14). Non-negotiable #21 requires a staff access to be traced, motivated and never silent: the permission is the *authority* for the read, and this is the *reason*.

A small enumeration on purpose. A free-text field alone collects "support" a thousand times and proves nothing; this is the half that can be counted, and X-Access-Reason is the half that is specific.

AccessReason.name: X-Access-Reason
AccessReason.description: The specific thing being looked into — a ticket reference, or a sentence. Eight characters minimum, because "x" is not a reason and a field that accepted it would collect nothing while looking like a control.

Error.description: The §10.4 envelope. Every failure has this shape, whatever produced it.

code.description: Stable and machine-readable. Branch on this, never on the message.

message.description: For a person. Wording may change without notice.

details.description: What the code could not say alone — the field at fault, the limit exceeded. Empty rather than absent.

request_id.description: Quote this when reporting a problem; the server log is keyed by it.

Money.description: Integer minor units and the currency. Never a float — a cent lost to binary rounding is a cent an auditor will ask about. The field is `minor_units` because the key this object sits under (`price`, `net`, `vat`, `gross`, `amount`) already says which amount it is; where money appears without such a key it is named in full instead, as `amount_minor_units` beside its own `currency`.

Product.description: `active` is deliberately absent: every product a caller can see is active, so the field would always be true and would only invite clients to branch on it.

ProductConfiguration.description: Free-form product settings. An object even when empty, so a client never has to tell `{}` from `null`.

rank.description: Orders plans against each other. An upgrade is a comparison of two ranks, never of two names (§13).

unit.description: Only a quota has one; the database refuses a unit on a boolean.

OfferGrant.description: What one offer version gives. A quota with no limit is `unlimited`, which is not the same as a limit of zero.

feature_id.description: The feature this grant is against. Present in the authoring view and absent from the sale view: ADR-033 freezes a published version, so changing what an offer grants means writing a new version from the old one — which needs the ids, not only the codes. A shop window read by strangers does not owe them the internal key of a catalogue row.

AuthoredOfferGrant.description: What one version of an offer grants, as its author sees it: the sale shape plus the feature's id.

billing_period.description: The same three the database allows. `ONE_OFF` was listed here and nowhere else — no migration, no domain code and no CHECK constraint has ever accepted it, so it promised a value the platform could not produce and a client that handled it was writing dead code.

valid_from.description: The window in which this version may be *sold* — not a subscription period, which §12 keeps separate.

version.description: Null only in principle — an offer is presented once a sellable version exists — but typed honestly rather than asserted away.

Subscriber.description: Who is bound. A seat names the person; a tenant subscription does not.

SubscriptionTerms.description: What a subscription commits to (§13.1). The distinction this exists to hold is the one that costs the most to lose: **the payment period is not the commitment**. A 24-month subscription billed monthly is one 24-month commitment billed 24 times, not 24 one-month subscriptions in a row.

term_months.description: How long the contract runs. Null is open-ended.

commitment_months.description: Never more than `term_months`; a commitment longer than the contract is not a commitment.

current_period_start.description: The *subscription's* period, which §12 keeps distinct from the offer's commercial window.

current_period_end.description: Null for a CUSTOM billing period, which has no end to be past.

CancellationDecision.description: Why the answer is what it is. What a customer needs is not `cancelled: true` but *when* it takes effect and which rule decided that (§13.1) — so the rule's id travels with the decision and the reasons are in plain words.

rule_id.description: Which rule decided. Stable, and the thing to quote in a support conversation.

chargeable_months.description: Months of the commitment still owed. Counted from the end of the period already paid for, not from today.

SubscriptionEvent.description: The history (§18). Every transition writes one, including those nobody performed — an expiry has no actor because the clock did it.

actor_user_id.description: Null when the clock did it rather than a person.

limit.description: Null means two different things, so `unlimited` says which.

source.description: What produced it — a subscription grant, or an override negotiated outside one.

PartySnapshot.description: Supplier or customer **as they were when the document was issued**, copied rather than referenced (§25). A later change of address must not rewrite an invoice already sent, and an RGPD erasure deliberately leaves this standing.

vat_rate_basis_points.description: Basis points, as stored. Sending "20%" would lose 5.5% to whatever the client's parser did with the half.

source_offer_version_id.description: Which offer version priced this line. Attribution runs through here, never through the subscription's *current* offer, which would credit today's offer with money an older one earned.

number.description: Null until issued. A draft has no legal number, and inventing a placeholder is how a gap enters a sequence that must not have one.

final.description: Whether it can still change. A final invoice is corrected by a credit note, never edited.

taxes.description: One row per jurisdiction and rate. They sum to the invoice's VAT — a test asserts it.

CreditNote.description: How a final invoice is corrected. Its own gapless sequence, separate from the invoices'.

direction.description: Always CREDIT. Present so a client reading a mixed ledger never has to infer the sign.

provider.description: Which PSP. The domain never names one; this is the adapter that was used.

final.description: Whether the status can still move. A webhook arriving after this is ignored rather than applied twice.

method.description: How it was paid. Never card data — §24 forbids storing that here at all.

failure_reason.description: The provider's category, never its raw message: that can carry an endpoint or a token, and this field is served over the API (§31).

Transmission.description: An invoice's journey to a certified e-invoicing platform (§25.1). Four states, and a rejection is a settled outcome rather than an error to retry blindly.

BillingProfile.description: Who the tenant is, for invoicing. Copied onto each document at issue — changing it never rewrites an invoice already sent.

Refund.description: A refund against a settled payment.

taxable_person.description: What the customer *claims*. Claiming it is not the same as proving it — see the status below.

vat_number_status.description: UNAVAILABLE is "we asked and got no answer" — not a refusal, and definitely not a verification. It is its own state because §25.2 has to be able to show it as an anomaly.

vat_number_verified_at.description: Evidence with a date on it. A number is re-checked when this gets old, not on every save.

reverse_charge_available.description: Only a *verified* business gets it. Fail-closed: an outage leaves the number unproved rather than trusted (R8).

TaxRate.description: Rates carry validity windows, so a correction closes one window and opens another instead of restating an invoice already issued (R7).

source.description: Where the figure came from. A paramétrage seed, not a fiscal authority.

TaxCalculation.description: Not just a number: which rule produced it, and why. An invoice priced under a regime the customer disputes is a conversation, and `reasons` is what that conversation needs.

legal_mention.description: The wording the invoice must carry when a regime requires one.

VatTransaction.description: The fiscal fact, written in the same transaction as the document that caused it — a sale whose VAT row could be lost is a sale that cannot be declared.

status.description: Closure is one-way, and a trigger enforces it: figures somebody has declared do not quietly change underneath them.

VatDeclaration.description: What was declared, frozen at closure. Reading a closed period reports this rather than recomputing — a recomputation would answer a different question than the one that was filed.

open.description: Whether it can still be accepted *now*. Derived from the clock, so an expired quote reads as closed without anything having had to sweep it.

offer_version_id.description: The version that priced it. Pinned, so a catalogue change cannot silently reprice a quote already sent.

Order.description: The payment gate is readable straight off the document: an `invoice_id` from fulfilment onwards, a `subscription_id` only once that invoice is paid. Both non-null is #20's chain complete.

quote_id.description: Null for an order placed directly, without a quote.

subscription_id.description: Appears only after the invoice is paid. Nothing is provisioned before the money arrives.

type.description: A dotted event name, so it reads as what happened rather than a label somebody invented at the call site.

legal_effect.description: When true the rendered text is kept as it was sent. "What did we say?" is half the question a pre-renewal notice has to answer, and paraphrasing it later from the payload is not an answer.

Delivery.description: One attempt on one channel. A failing channel must not lose the notification, and a succeeding one must not make the others look sent.

status.description: SENDING means a runner holds it under a lease. That state is what makes a duplicate send impossible rather than unlikely (R12).

suppression_reason.description: Present exactly when suppressed. Writing nothing would make "did we tell them?" unanswerable.

failure_reason.description: The class of the error, never its message: a provider's message can carry an endpoint or a token, and this field is served over the API (§31).

Consent.description: Revocation is a date, not a deletion. Erasing the row would destroy the record that permission once existed, which is the opposite of proof.

source.description: How it was obtained — the evidence, not just the claim.

schema_version.description: Which document shape this is. Enforced on write (non-negotiable #10): an unknown version is refused rather than stored and puzzled over later.

deleted_at.description: When somebody deleted it, or null while it is live. A deleted project keeps its versions, its assets and every job that referred to it — deletion is a date, not a cascade (R13).

ProjectDocument.description: The JSONB document. Key order is preserved and insignificant whitespace is gone — what is stored is what comes back, which is the guarantee snapshot and restore rest on. Large assets are refused here and belong in storage (non-negotiable #9).

content_type.description: The **sniffed** type, not the one the request claimed. A client that says image/png about a script is not believed.

checksum.description: Of the stored bytes, so a corrupted download is detectable.

kind.description: A composite foreign key confines platform staff to SUPPORT threads, so staff cannot be added to an internal one even by a bug.

unread.description: For the caller, counted from their own watermark. Absent where the reader is not a participant.

seq.description: Per thread and consecutive. A deleted message keeps its place, so the sequence never develops a hole where a reply used to be.

author_kind.description: A foreign key ties the author to a participant *of that kind*, so a message from somebody who was never in the thread cannot be written at all.

body.description: Empty when deleted, or when the author was erased under RGPD.

last_read_seq.description: The watermark. It never goes backwards — marking an older message read cannot un-read a newer one.

may_author_offers.description: Whether the platform has lent this tenant the catalogue. False by default: offers are keyed on product, not tenant, so a tenant administrator editing them changes what every other customer of that product is sold on. When false, `catalog.manage` is not resolved for this tenant's members at all.

StaffTenant.description: A tenant as the platform sees it: the tenant, and the products it holds (ADR-047). `products` is the platform’s answer — which products it has assigned this tenant, through the console — so it lives on the staff shape and not on the `Tenant` a tenant reads about itself.

products.description: In code order. A retired product a tenant still holds is listed with `active: false`.

StaffAccessEntry.description: Non-negotiable #21: a staff read of a tenant's data is never silent. Written in the same transaction as the read it records.

purpose.description: Why the read happened (R14). Null on rows written before R14, and on reads that cross no boundary — listing a queue, reading this log. Null means "not recorded", never "no reason".

reason.description: The specific reference the person gave.

result.description: What the handler reported — how many rows moved, not the rows.

run_after.description: Work waits for this. A delayed run is late rather than wrong.

failure_reason.description: A category. The driver's account of what failed goes to the log, never here (§31).

AuditEntry.description: §30's trail. Append-only, and the one permitted update clears the actor and nothing else — what happened is kept, who did it can be forgotten.

actor.description: Carries both the id and whether it was erased, so an act nobody performed stays distinguishable from one whose performer has since been forgotten. Collapsing them into a bare null would turn every erasure into a system action.

GeoJsonPolygon.description: A GeoJSON Polygon with **exactly one linear ring** and no Z ordinate — narrower than RFC 7946 on purpose. The phase 1 spatial backend is core PostgreSQL (§19), whose `polygon` type has no holes and no third dimension, and the tempting repairs — keep the outer ring, drop the elevation — answer a different question from the one that was asked. A ring with a hole, a MultiPolygon or a 3D position is refused with 400 rather than reduced.

coordinates.description: One ring, closed: its last position repeats its first, so a triangle has four positions. At most 513 positions, and the ring must be simple — a self-intersecting ring is refused with 422, because PostgreSQL measures a bowtie as zero area rather than as an error.

CoordinateReference.description:
Which kind of coordinates the geometry is in. Required, and never inferred: a parcel in Lambert-93 and the same parcel in WGS 84 are both pairs of finite numbers, and guessing from magnitude would report a 1200 m² plot as 0.00000015.

`PROJECTED` — a planar system in linear units (Lambert-93, a UTM zone). Lengths and areas are in those units; the platform never learns which unit and never claims one.

`GEOGRAPHIC` — longitude and latitude in degrees. Topology is answerable, so `/geometry/intersections` accepts it and withholds `distance`. `/geometry/measure` refuses it with 422: a degree of longitude is not a fixed distance, so an area in degrees is not an area.

BoundingBox.description: The axis-aligned extent, in the coordinate units of the input.

Measurement.description: Area and perimeter in the coordinate units of the input, squared and plain respectively. There is no unit field because there is no unit to report: the caller chose the projection and knows whether it is metres or feet, and inventing "m²" for a US state plane would be a claim this platform cannot support.

vertices.description: Corners of the ring, counting the closing position once.

SpatialRelation.description: How the subject stands to one candidate. Four answers rather than one, because a parcel search needs to separate the plots a footprint merely clips from the ones it swallows whole — and the plot that swallows the footprint is a third answer.

id.description: The id the caller gave this candidate.

intersects.description: Whether the shapes share any point. Genuinely geometric, not a bounding-box approximation: an L-shaped parcel and a block sitting in its notch have overlapping boxes and this answers false.

contains.description: Whether the subject wholly contains the candidate. Always false for a point subject.

within.description: Whether the subject lies wholly inside the candidate.

distance.description: Minimum separation in the input's linear units, zero when the shapes touch. **Null when `crs` is GEOGRAPHIC**, where a separation in degrees is not a distance. Null rather than absent, so one response shape serves both references.

OfferDraft.description: The terms of a version being written. Always born `DRAFT` — no field here can say otherwise, because publishing is a separate and deliberate act.

price_minor_units.description: Zero is legitimate: a free tier is still an offer.

valid_from.description: When this version may start being sold. Defaults to now. Not the subscriber's period — §12 keeps the two apart.

valid_until.description: When it stops being sellable. Null leaves the window open.

grants.description: What this version entitles the subscriber to.

feature_id.description: A feature of this product. One belonging to another product is refused, not ignored.

limit.description: Null means unlimited for a quota, and is the only valid value for a boolean capability.

AuthoredOfferVersion.description: A version as its author sees it, carrying the status the sale view has no reason to mention.

version.description: Assigned by the database as `max + 1`, never by the caller.

AuthoredOffer.description: An offer with every version it has, drafts included.

code.description: How documents name this offer. Not editable: an identifier that can change is not an identifier.

publicly_listed.description: Whether the public storefront advertises this offer. Distinct from being on sale: a price negotiated with one reseller is sellable and is nobody else’s business. Only `staff.catalog.manage` may change it.

DirectoryEnvelope.description: One page and how much lies behind it. The total is counted rather than inferred from a short page — an operator needs to know whether they are looking at forty customers or four thousand, and "the page came back short" answers that only on the last one.

erased_at.description: Set means anonymised: the identity is gone and the record is kept.

Skin.description:
How a tenant wants this product to look. Every field is present and null when unset, rather than absent — a client reading this to decide how to render needs one shape, and null means "use the product's defaults".

Kept per (tenant, product): §12.1 lets one tenant use several products, and a company white-labelling two of them has no reason to want the same shade in both.

primary_color.description: Lower-case hex. The database refuses anything else: these values end up in a stylesheet, and a colour column accepting arbitrary text is a stylesheet injection with extra steps.

logo_asset_id.description: An asset, fetched through the usual signed-link route. Storing the logo as an asset means it goes through the same sniffing and the same SVG refusal as every other upload.

CheckoutSession.description:
**A checkout session is an order.** There is no `checkout_sessions` table and no separate lifecycle: `id` is the order's id, and everything a session would hold — is it paid, what was invoiced, did the subscription start — already lives on the order, the invoice and the payment. A second row tracking the same thing is a second answer that can disagree with the first, and the first is the one the money is attached to.

`status` is derived on read for the same reason, never stored.

order_id.description: The same value as `id`, said plainly.

status.description: `PAYMENT_FAILED` means the order still awaits payment and the last attempt is dead — the state a retry exists for. Reporting it as AWAITING_PAYMENT would hide that nothing is coming.

invoice_id.description: Null only for an order with nothing to collect — a free offer.

subscription_id.description: Set once the money arrived: activation is payment-gated, so this stays null while the invoice is unpaid.

access_token.description: Present it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Hold it in memory; it is short-lived by design.

expires_in.description: Seconds from now. A duration rather than an instant, so a browser with a skewed clock still schedules its renewal correctly.

Session.description: The refresh token is deliberately absent: it leaves in an `HttpOnly` cookie that no script can read, and putting it here as well would throw away the reason the cookie exists.

StaffMember.description: One person holding a platform role. `email` and `display_name` are null once §26's erasure has emptied them; the row stays, because authority nobody can see is authority nobody can revoke.

PlatformRole.description: A grantable platform role, as the database holds it.

StaffRoster.description: The whole roster and the roles that may be granted. Returned by the two writes as well as the read, so a screen's next state is never guessed from a status code.

PlatformProduct.description: A product as the platform’s own administrator sees it. `active` appears here and nowhere else, because every other product shape has already filtered on it — the context chain treats an inactive product as absent, and so does the storefront.

code.description: What clients send as `X-Product` and the storefront takes as `?product=`. Chosen once, at creation, and never editable: an identifier that can change is not an identifier.

active.description: A retired product keeps its tenants, subscriptions and invoices; what changes is that every door into it is closed.

PaymentProviderClient.description: What the page needs to *use* a `client_secret` (ADR-048): which provider, the key that loads its own component, and whether any of this moves real money. Null when there is no payment to make (a free offer) or when the provider has no page-side part (the stub). `publishable_key` is designed by the provider to sit in a page and is not a secret — it belongs in the contract rather than in a build variable, which would freeze one deployment’s key into a bundle another deployment reuses.

name.description: The provider’s stable name, as `payments.provider` records it.

sandbox.description: True when no real money moves: a test mode, a sandbox, a stub. The screen says so, because a demo on real cards and a production on test cards are the two mistakes that cost the most.

BillingSupplier.description: The mandatory mentions of an invoice's issuer (§25). Every field is present in a response, null included, so a form binding to it finds the same shape whether the product was configured years ago or never. `legal_name` and `country_code` are the two an invoice cannot be issued without — a supplier not liable for VAT legitimately has no number, and requiring one would exclude a whole class of French business.

vat_number.description: Null for a supplier under the franchise en base, which invoices perfectly legally without one.

country_code.description: Two letters, ISO 3166-1, upper-cased on the way in. It decides the VAT regime the invoice is issued under, so a value that is not a country code is refused rather than normalised — a guessed jurisdiction files somebody's VAT in the wrong country.

TaxSettings.description: The supplier's own fiscal position. §25.3 requires it to be configured and never derived: whether the supplier is registered for the One Stop Shop is a dated fact about the business, and crossing the distance-selling threshold changes the regime of subsequent sales only — deriving it from turnover would retroactively restate invoices already issued.

country.description: The jurisdiction VAT is filed in. Defaults to the billing supplier's country when the key has never been written.

oss_registered.description: Decides how a cross-border consumer sale is taxed.

supply_type.description: What is being supplied changes the place of taxation, so it is stated rather than assumed.

currency.description: The currency this product sells in.

SetupStep.description: One link in the chain a product has to complete before it can sell. Carries **facts, not sentences**: `key` names the step and `detail` carries what was counted or found missing, so the words belong to whatever renders it, in whatever language that surface speaks.

key.description: Stable identifier. The array's order is the dependency order: following it top to bottom never meets a refusal.

blocking.description: Whether a sale is impossible until this step is done. `tax` and `features` are listed and are not blocking — a supplier selling at home invoices correctly without a stated tax position, and an offer granting only access to the product is a legitimate offer.

detail.description: What was counted or found missing — `count`, `missing`, `code`, `active`, `country` depending on the step. An object even when empty, so a client never has to tell `{}` from `null`.

DemoWorld.description: What the demonstration world contains once it has been seeded — the answer the console shows so somebody can sign back in, since resetting deletes every account including the caller's. The password is not a secret: it is in this platform's source.

holds.description: The product codes this organisation holds (ADR-047).

people.description: One person per role the platform defines.

role.description: A tenant role code or a platform role code, by scope.

tenants.description: Slugs of the organisations a tenant-role holder is a member of; empty for platform staff.

password.description: The one password every seeded person signs in with.

invoices.description: The legal numbers of the invoices the seeded subscriptions raised.

Unauthenticated.description: No credential, or one that did not verify.

PermissionDenied.description: Authenticated, but not allowed to do this here.

NotFound.description: No such thing — or none this caller may see. The two are deliberately indistinguishable.

TooManyRequests.description: The caller has spent its allowance for the current window (§31).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. A client told only "too many" would guess, and a guessing client retries too soon.

InternalError.description: A controlled 500 (§37.9). The diagnostic detail is in the server log against this request_id, never on the wire.

NotConfigured.description: This deployment cannot issue sessions: no signing secret is configured.

get.description: Behind its own permission, and separate from the tenant surfaces entirely (#19).

post.summary: Forget a person, keeping what the law requires
post.description:
Non-negotiables #14 and #15. The person is **anonymised, never deleted** — the schema forbids the alternative: of twenty foreign keys into users, five RESTRICT and four CASCADE, so a delete would either be refused or would silently take notification history with it.

The response is the receipt. What was kept is counted and justified per category, because afterwards the question is not "did you delete everything?" — it did not, deliberately — but "what did you keep, and on what ground?"

**The invoice still names them afterwards.** Altering an issued invoice falsifies a legal document, which is a worse answer than keeping it.

200.description: What was erased, and what was kept and why.

409.description: Already erased. A second run would file a second, emptier account of the same act.

get.description:
`/admin/metrics` answers "how much"; this answers "which ones", which is the question an unpaid balance actually raises.

Requires `admin.finance.read`.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: One customer.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: DRAFT, ISSUED, PAID, CANCELLED, CREDITED.

get.description:
`/admin/queue` answers whether the runner is alive (R10); this answers what it is carrying, which is the next question when the answer to the first is "yes, and something is still wrong".

**The payload is deliberately not returned.** It is whatever the caller handed the queue, it can carry anything, and "which jobs are stuck" does not need to know what is inside them.

Requires `admin.health.read`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: PENDING, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The handler's name.

get.description:
Read from monthly rollups, never recomputed over the ledger — a dashboard that scans every transaction gets slower every month it succeeds (§25.2).

**Turnover is what was invoiced, not what was collected**, and currency is part of the grain: €100 and $100 are never added. A renewal rate is *null* when nothing came up for renewal, because zero would claim everybody left.

The product is named in the query because an admin surface resolves none of its own.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Which month the offers are ranked within. Top offers over a year and over last month are different questions.

get.summary: Whether the job queue is still being polled
get.description:
A quiet queue and a cron that stopped firing produce the same silence, and this is what tells them apart (R10).

Three signals, because they are three different things to go and fix: `seconds_since_finished` ageing is a cron that stopped; an ageing `oldest_unfinished_seconds` is a runner that died mid-pass; a growing backlog while the clock looks healthy is a wedged handler.

**No staleness verdict is invented.** How often cron fires is deployment configuration this process does not know, so `stale` appears only when `?stale_after=` supplies the expectation.

parameters.name: stale_after
parameters.description: Seconds. Supplying it asks for a verdict; omitting it asks only for the clock.

post.description: Takes no body: the credential is the `HttpOnly` cookie, which the browser attaches by itself. A body field would mean a script had read the token, which is what the cookie exists to prevent. The refresh token is rotated on every call, so presenting a spent one is evidence of a copy and revokes every session for the account.

409.description: The invoice is not issued, or has already been transmitted.

Including why it failed, as a code and a category — never the provider's raw message, which can carry an endpoint or a token (§31).

202.description: The refund, accepted by the provider.

409.description: Not refundable — unsettled, or already fully refunded.

422.description: The amount exceeds what remains.

422.description: A field was present but unacceptable — a country code that is not two letters, say.

post.summary: Buy an offer in one call
post.description:
Places the order, raises its invoice and asks the provider to authorize — three calls a client could already make. What this adds is that the client no longer orchestrates them, and that a dropped connection leaves an order they can look up rather than a charge nobody can account for.

**The body names an offer and nothing else.** No amount, because a client that could name a figure could name a smaller one; the price is the offer's. No instrument, because the customer gives that to the provider directly — card data never reaches this platform's database (§24).

**It does not start the subscription.** That waits for the money, through the same webhook everything else arrives by. A checkout that activated on creation would extend credit to anyone who can reach this endpoint.

offer_id.description: An offer on sale in this product right now. A draft, an expired one, or one belonging to another product is not found.

201.description: The session, with the client secret if there is anything to pay.

client_secret.description: Handed to the payment provider’s client SDK. **Returned here and nowhere else**: it is short-lived and it is a credential, so it is never stored (§31). Null when the provider uses a redirect rather than a secret. A caller who needs a fresh one retries the payment, which is a new attempt and gets its own.

404.description: No such offer on sale in this product.

409.description: `BILLING_PROFILE_REQUIRED` — the tenant has no billing profile, so nothing can be invoiced to it. Refused before any document is raised, because numbering is gapless.

422.description: `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_REFUSED` — the provider would not start this payment; `details.provider_code` carries its reason, written for operators. Or `PAYMENT_AMOUNT_UNSUPPORTED` — an amount the provider cannot represent in this currency.

503.description: `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_REJECTED_KEY` or `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_UNREACHABLE` — this deployment’s provider credentials were refused, or the provider could not be reached. Configuration, not the caller’s doing.

get.description:
The status is derived from the order and its latest payment rather than stored: the order knows whether it completed, the payment knows whether money moved, and a third status written down could disagree with both.

No `client_secret` — there is nothing to return it from.

get.summary: Fetch a file's bytes with a signed link
get.description:
The only endpoint that returns something other than JSON, and one of four reachable with no credential — because the **link** carries the authority. It is minted with an expiry and a signature, and this verifies both before a byte is served.

That is why it lives under a public prefix and why nothing may be mounted there that does not authenticate its own request. An expired or tampered link is a 403 with no detail: telling a probing caller which half was wrong is telling them how to fix it.

`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` is set deliberately. The stored content type was sniffed from the bytes on upload rather than taken from the uploader's claim, and this stops a browser second-guessing that and executing something as a different type.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The signature minted by /assets/{assetId}/link. It carries its own expiry.

200.description: The file. Served as an attachment, with the sniffed content type and a sanitised filename.

Content-Type.description: The type sniffed at upload, never the one the uploader claimed.

X-Content-Type-Options.description: Stops a browser overriding the sniffed type and running the file as something else.

403.description: The link expired, or its signature did not verify. No detail: a probing caller learns nothing from it.

get.summary: What the tenant is entitled to
get.description: Resolved from what is in force now, so a lapsed subscription grants nothing without anything having had to sweep it first. This is the *tenant's* view: a seat held by one colleague still appears here, which is a known gap rather than a design.
The vocabulary entitlements are expressed in. A quota carries its unit; a boolean must not.

post.summary: One shape against a set of candidate polygons
post.description:
Answers overlap, containment and proximity for each candidate, in the order they were sent. The candidates carry ids the caller chose and those ids come straight back, which is what makes this usable against a parcel register the platform has never seen: the caller holds the mapping and this side holds none of it.

A polygon subject asks what a footprint touches; a point subject asks which parcel holds an address. Accepted in either coordinate reference, because topology does not depend on the unit — but `distance` is withheld in degrees.

candidates.description: The parcels to test against. Ids must be distinct — two rows sharing one id would make the response impossible to index by, so a repeat is refused rather than resolved.

200.description: One relation per candidate, in the order given.

400.description: A geometry this backend does not represent, a candidate without an id, or two candidates sharing one.

422.description: `GEOMETRY_NOT_SIMPLE` — a ring crosses itself.

post.summary: Area, perimeter and extent of a polygon
post.description:
Pure computation: no row is read and none is written, and two tenants asking the same question get the same answer. The door is the `gis.access` **entitlement** rather than a permission — what the plan bought, not what the role allows (§10.2) — which is why the refusal here is 403 `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED` and never 404.

Requires projected coordinates; see `CoordinateReference` for why degrees are refused rather than converted.

400.description: The geometry is not one this backend represents: a hole, a MultiPolygon, a Z ordinate, a ring that is not closed, or an unknown `crs`.

422.description: `GEOMETRY_NOT_SIMPLE` — the ring crosses itself, which has no well-defined area. Or `PROJECTION_REQUIRED` — `crs` was GEOGRAPHIC.

get.description: The one path reachable with no credential at all. It answers from the process alone: an unreachable database must not make the process look dead to an orchestrator, so this stays up when data is down.

One call, because an offer with no version has no price and no terms — nothing can be sold, shown or quoted from it. Born `DRAFT`; publishing is a separate act.

Behind `catalog.manage`, not `catalog.read`: reading what is on sale is something every member does, deciding what it costs is not.

400.description: The name is missing or blank.

404.description: No such offer in this product.

post.description:
The version is named in the body rather than the path because an offer can hold several drafts, and "publish the offer" would have to guess which one.

Two versions of one offer may not be on sale over the same period. That is an exclusion constraint in the database, not a check in the service, so it holds against concurrent publishes as well as careless ones.

400.description: No version given.

404.description: No such offer in this product.

post.description:
§12 as an endpoint: a change of price, quota or features **creates a version rather than rewriting history**. There is deliberately no way to edit a published version's price, so this is the only way to change what an offer costs.

The version number is not in the body — it is `max + 1`, assigned by the statement that writes the row, so two authors working at once get 4 and 5 rather than a collision.

201.description: The offer, with the new draft.

400.description: The body is not a valid draft.

404.description: No such offer in this product, or a granted feature is not this product's.

post.description:
A **new** payment against the same invoice, never a resurrection of the old one. `PaymentStatus` is deliberately one-way and says why: the customer may have used a different instrument, and two attempts that must be told apart cannot share a provider reference.

Refused while the previous attempt is still in flight — a second authorization then risks collecting twice for one debt — and refused if it succeeded, where there is nothing to retry.

sellable.description: True when no blocking step remains.

next.description: The key of the first blocking step, or null when nothing blocks — which is what lets a screen say "done" rather than point at nowhere.

400.description: `VALIDATION_FAILED` — no `product` was named.
